title: Memory Loss

rationale.TSH / B12 / RPR: Rule out reversible causes of dementia.
rationale.Cholinesterase inhibitor (Donepezil): First-line for mild-mod AD. Modest symptomatic benefit.
rationale.Caregiver support / Advance care plannin: Safety, driving, home support, legal planning.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with progressive episodic memory loss (recent > remote), difficulty with word finding, visuospatial deficits, apraxia, and decline in executive function, gradually worsening over months to years. Alzheimer's disease is the most common cause of dementia. Pathophysiology: accumulation of extracellular beta-amyloid plaques and intracellular neurofibrillary tangles (hyperphosphorylated tau protein) → neuronal death. Rule out reversible causes: B12 deficiency, hypothyroidism (TSH), neurosyphilis (RPR), normal pressure hydrocephalus, depression (pseudodementia). Imaging: CT/MRI brain shows diffuse cortical atrophy (especially medial temporal/hippocampal). Diagnosis is clinical — supportive features. MMSE or MOCA for cognitive screening. Treatment: cholinesterase inhibitors (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine) for mild-mod AD. Memantine (NMDA antagonist) for mod-severe. Both provide modest symptomatic benefit — no disease-modifying therapy currently. Caregiver support, advance care planning, safety assessment.
